question: A cloud team must prove to auditors that storage buckets stay encrypted and never become public, and the CISO also wants an outside party to confirm the controls work. Which practices together meet both goals? (Choose two.)

choices.a: A tool that continuously evaluates cloud resource settings against compliance rules and alerts on drift
choices.b: A periodic review of the controls by an external auditor
choices.c: An annual policy acknowledgement signed by each cloud engineer
choices.d: A self-assessment questionnaire completed by the cloud team each quarter

explanation: Automated compliance monitoring checks configurations continuously and flags drift as soon as it happens, and an external auditor provides independent confirmation that the controls work. A policy acknowledgement shows that staff agreed to rules but does not check settings, and a self-assessment is neither continuous nor independent.

question: A U.S. company sells online to customers in several U.S. states and in the European Union. Which statement best describes the privacy laws it must consider?

choices.a: Only the privacy laws of the country where the company is headquartered apply
choices.b: Only the privacy laws of the location where its servers are hosted apply
choices.c: It may be subject at the same time to state or regional laws, national laws, and laws such as GDPR that protect EU residents regardless of where the company is located
choices.d: Federal law always replaces state and foreign privacy laws, so only federal rules apply

explanation: Privacy obligations are layered: local or regional laws, national laws, and global regulations such as GDPR, which applies to organizations that offer goods or services to people in the EU, can all apply at once. Headquarters location and server location do not limit which laws apply, and federal law does not automatically replace state or foreign privacy laws.

question: Under privacy regulations such as GDPR, which term describes the identified or identifiable living person whose personal data is collected and processed?
explanation: The data subject is the individual the personal data is about, and privacy laws give that person rights over the data. The controller decides why and how the data is processed, the processor handles it on the controller's behalf, and a custodian manages the data day to day.

question: A company's vice president of sales is accountable for the customer contact database. She decides how it is classified and must approve any new access to it, while the IT team manages its backups and encryption. Which role does the vice president hold for this data?
explanation: The data owner is the senior person accountable for a data set, who sets its classification and approves access. The IT team acts as custodian by carrying out technical protection. A processor is a separate party that processes personal data for a controller, and data subjects are the customers described in the records.

question: A privacy officer finds personal data about customers who closed their accounts twelve years ago scattered across file shares and backups, even though no law or business need requires keeping it. Which actions best address this? (Choose two.)

choices.a: Build a data inventory that identifies what personal data the company holds and where it is stored
choices.b: Adopt a data retention policy that sets how long each type of data is kept and when it must be disposed of
choices.c: Increase the backup frequency so the old records are protected more often
choices.d: Place all of the old records under legal hold

explanation: A data inventory shows what personal data exists and where, and a retention policy sets how long each data type is kept and when it is securely disposed of, so data is not kept longer than needed. More frequent backups would create more copies of data that should be removed, and a legal hold is only for data relevant to litigation or an investigation, which is not described here.

question: A former customer in the European Union asks an online retailer to erase all personal data it holds about her, because she no longer uses the service and withdraws her consent. Which privacy right is she exercising?
explanation: The right to be forgotten, also called the right to erasure, lets a data subject ask for personal data to be deleted when there is no longer a valid reason to keep it. Data portability means receiving data in a reusable format, the right of access means obtaining a copy of the data, and rectification means correcting inaccurate data.

question: Before the annual external audit, a company's internal audit staff test whether departments are following the organization's own security policies and the regulations that apply to it, and they report gaps to management. What is the main purpose of this activity?

choices.a: To provide an independent opinion that customers and regulators can rely on
choices.b: To verify internal compliance with policies and regulations and find gaps before outside auditors do
choices.c: To simulate an attacker's attempt to breach the network
choices.d: To replace the need for any external audit

explanation: An internal compliance audit checks that the organization follows its own policies and the regulations it is subject to, so gaps can be fixed early. It is not independent of the organization, so it does not replace an external audit or provide an outside opinion. Simulating an attacker is the job of a penetration test.

question: Which group, usually a subcommittee of the board of directors, oversees the internal audit function, reviews audit findings, and manages the relationship with the external auditors?
explanation: The audit committee is a board-level group that provides oversight of internal and external audits and makes sure findings are addressed. A change advisory board approves changes, an incident response team handles security incidents, and a SOC monitors and responds to security events.

question: Each quarter, department managers complete a questionnaire rating how well their own teams meet each control in the company's security framework, and the results are used to prioritize improvements. Which type of assessment is this?
explanation: In a self-assessment, the organization evaluates its own controls, often with questionnaires or checklists, which is quick and inexpensive but not independent. An independent third-party audit and a regulatory examination are performed by outside parties, and a penetration test actively tries to exploit weaknesses.

question: Examiners from a government banking agency arrive at a bank to review its information security program, interview staff, and check its controls against the agency's rules. Which type of audit or assessment is taking place?
explanation: A regulatory examination is an external review performed by a government regulator with authority over the organization, and it checks compliance with that regulator's requirements. An internal audit and a self-assessment are performed by the organization itself, and a penetration test actively tries to exploit vulnerabilities instead of reviewing compliance.

question: A company hires an outside consulting firm to evaluate its security program against the NIST Cybersecurity Framework, identify gaps, and recommend improvements. No regulator is involved. Which type of review is this?
explanation: An external assessment is an evaluation performed by a party outside the organization, such as a consulting firm measuring the program against a framework. A self-assessment and an internal audit are performed by the organization's own staff, and a regulatory examination is conducted by a government regulator.

question: A tester is hired to see whether she can enter a company's data center by following employees through badge-controlled doors, cloning access badges, and bypassing door locks. Which type of penetration test is this?
explanation: A physical penetration test checks physical controls such as doors, locks, badge readers, and the staff who are supposed to stop tailgating. Defensive testing focuses on detecting and responding to attacks, and integrated testing combines attackers and defenders. Unknown environment describes how much information the tester gets, not what is tested.

question: During a security exercise, one team uses real-world adversary tactics to break into the network, move laterally, and reach the customer database without the security operations staff being told the timing. Which type of penetration testing is this team performing?
explanation: Offensive penetration testing, often called red teaming, emulates real attackers to find and exploit weaknesses. Defensive testing focuses on detecting and stopping attacks, integrated testing has attackers and defenders work together openly, and passive reconnaissance only gathers public information without touching the target.

question: During an attack simulation, a team of security analysts is responsible for watching alerts, detecting the simulated attackers' activity, containing compromised hosts, and improving monitoring rules based on what they missed. Which type of penetration testing role does this team represent?
explanation: Defensive penetration testing, often called blue teaming, focuses on detecting, responding to, and defending against attacks, and on improving those defenses. Offensive testing is the attacking side, physical testing targets facilities and physical controls, and known environment describes how much information the testers are given.

question: A company wants its attack testers and its SOC analysts to work side by side. As each attack technique is run, the testers explain what they did and the analysts immediately check whether it was detected and tune their alerts. Which type of penetration testing is this?
explanation: Integrated penetration testing, often called purple teaming, combines offensive and defensive teams and has them share information in real time to improve detection quickly. Purely offensive or purely defensive testing keeps the teams separate, and unknown environment describes how much information the testers receive.

question: Before a penetration test of a web application, the testers receive the source code, architecture diagrams, and administrator credentials so they can review everything in depth. Which type of test environment is this?
explanation: In a known environment test, formerly called white box, testers receive full details such as code, diagrams, and credentials, which allows thorough coverage. A partially known environment test gives only limited information, an unknown environment test gives none, and passive reconnaissance is an information-gathering technique, not a test environment.

question: A company gives penetration testers its internal IP address ranges and a standard employee account, but no network diagrams, source code, or administrator credentials. Which type of test environment is this?
explanation: A partially known environment test, formerly called gray box, gives the testers some information, such as address ranges or a low-privilege account, often to simulate an insider or an attacker who has gained a foothold. A known environment test provides full details, an unknown environment test provides none, and integrated describes cooperation between attackers and defenders.

question: Leadership wants a penetration test that most realistically shows what an outside attacker could do with no inside knowledge. The testers will be given only the company's name. Which type of test environment should be used?
explanation: An unknown environment test, formerly called black box, gives testers no internal information, so they must discover everything as an external attacker would. Known and partially known environment tests provide full or partial information in advance, and defensive testing focuses on detecting and responding to attacks.

question: An accounts payable clerk receives an email that appears to come from the CEO. Which characteristics most strongly indicate a phishing attempt? (Choose two.)

choices.a: The display name is the CEO's, but the reply-to address is on a free webmail domain
choices.b: It urgently asks the clerk to buy gift cards before the end of the day and to tell no one
choices.c: It refers to a staff meeting that is already on the clerk's calendar
choices.d: It was sent during normal business hours

explanation: A mismatch between the display name and the actual or reply-to address, and urgent, secretive requests for gift cards or payments, are classic signs of phishing and business email compromise. Mentioning a real meeting and arriving during business hours are normal traits and do not indicate phishing.

question: A user clicks the report-phishing button on a suspicious email. What should the security team do next?

choices.a: Reply to the sender to ask whether the message is legitimate
choices.b: Delete the reporter's copy and close the ticket
choices.c: Analyze the message and, if it is malicious, remove matching copies from other mailboxes and block its sender and links
choices.d: Forward the original message, with its live links, to all staff as a warning

explanation: Reported messages should be analyzed, and if they are malicious, the team should find and purge other copies, block the indicators, and give the reporter feedback. Replying to the sender confirms the address is active, deleting only one copy leaves others exposed, and forwarding live links spreads the threat.

question: A user knows it is against policy but regularly disables his endpoint protection so that unapproved software will install, and he copies work files to his personal cloud storage so he can work from home. Which category of anomalous behavior does this represent?
explanation: Risky behavior is when a user knowingly takes actions that increase risk, such as bypassing security tools or moving data to unapproved locations. Unintentional behavior is an honest mistake, and unexpected behavior is activity that departs from a user's normal pattern. Insider recruitment is not one of the anomalous behavior categories.

question: An accountant who normally works weekday business hours signs in at 3 AM on a Sunday and starts downloading files from an engineering source code repository she has never used before. Which category of anomalous behavior does this best represent?
explanation: Unexpected behavior is activity that differs from a user's normal pattern, such as unusual hours or access to resources unrelated to the job, and it should be reported and investigated. Unintentional behavior is an obvious mistake, and risky behavior is a user knowingly breaking rules in a way that adds risk. Nothing about this activity fits acceptable use.

question: Which situations are examples of unintentional anomalous behavior? (Choose two.)

choices.a: Email autocomplete causes an employee to send a customer spreadsheet to an outside contact with a similar name
choices.b: An administrator accidentally makes a cloud file share public while troubleshooting a permissions problem
choices.c: A user signs in from another country one hour after signing in from the office
choices.d: An employee deliberately turns off the host firewall to play an online game

explanation: Unintentional behavior is a mistake made without intent to cause harm, such as sending data to the wrong recipient or misconfiguring permissions by accident. A sign-in from another country an hour later is unexpected behavior that suggests compromised credentials, and deliberately disabling a firewall is risky behavior.

question: A new employee is unsure whether she may store work documents in her personal cloud storage account. Where should she look first for the organization's rule?

choices.a: The acceptable use policy in the employee handbook

explanation: Policies and handbooks, such as the acceptable use policy, give users written guidance on what is and is not allowed with company data and systems. An incident response playbook guides responders during incidents, SIEM rules are technical detection logic, and a vendor SLA defines service levels, not employee behavior.

question: A training module teaches employees to notice who is behind them at badge-controlled doors, to watch for people looking at their screens in public places, and to question unfamiliar people in restricted areas. Which user guidance topic is this?
explanation: Situational awareness training teaches people to pay attention to their surroundings so they notice tailgating, shoulder surfing, and unauthorized people. Password management covers creating and storing credentials, removable media training covers drives and cables, and operational security focuses on protecting information about the organization's activities from being gathered by adversaries.

question: An employee notices that a coworker who recently complained about being passed over for promotion has been asking for access to files outside his role and copying large amounts of data to a USB drive. According to insider threat training, what should the employee do?

choices.a: Confront the coworker and demand an explanation
choices.b: Report the concerns through the organization's designated reporting channel
choices.c: Log in to the coworker's email to look for evidence
choices.d: Ignore it, because the coworker is a trusted employee

explanation: Insider threat training teaches employees to recognize warning signs and report them through the proper channel, such as security or HR, so trained staff can investigate. Confronting the coworker could alert him and escalate the situation, accessing his email is unauthorized, and ignoring warning signs because of trust is how insider incidents go undetected.

question: Which practice should password management training recommend to employees?

choices.a: Reuse one strong password for both work and personal accounts so it is easy to remember
choices.b: Use the same base password and change one character for each site
choices.c: Use an approved password manager to create a long, unique password for each account and enable MFA where it is available
choices.d: Write passwords on a note kept in a locked desk drawer

explanation: A password manager makes it practical to use long, unique passwords everywhere, and MFA adds protection if a password is stolen. Reusing a password, even with small changes, lets one breach expose many accounts, and written passwords can be found by anyone who gets into the desk.

question: Which behaviors should removable media and cables training encourage? (Choose two.)

choices.a: Hand any USB drive found on company property to the security team without connecting it
choices.b: Charge devices only with company-issued or personally owned cables and chargers, not unknown cables or public USB ports
choices.c: Plug an unknown USB drive into a personal laptop instead of a work laptop to see who owns it
choices.d: Use a charging cable left in a conference room if it looks like a well-known brand

explanation: Found drives can carry malware that runs when connected, so they should be turned in without being plugged in, and unknown cables or public USB ports can be modified to inject keystrokes or steal data. Plugging a found drive into any computer, including a personal one, risks infection, and a malicious cable can look exactly like a brand-name one.

question: An employee receives a phone call from someone claiming to be from the IT help desk, who says the employee's mailbox is corrupted and asks for the MFA code just sent to the employee's phone. What should social engineering training tell the employee to do?

choices.a: Read the code to the caller, since only IT staff know about the mailbox
choices.b: Give the code only if the caller can state the employee's job title
choices.c: Ask the caller to send the request by email instead
choices.d: Refuse to share the code, end the call, and contact the help desk using the number in the company directory

explanation: MFA codes should never be shared, and callback verification using a known, trusted number defeats impersonation and vishing attempts. Details such as a job title are easy to find publicly, and an email request could come from the same attacker, so neither proves who the caller is.

question: An intern posts a team photo on social media to celebrate a product launch. The background shows a whiteboard with an internal network diagram and several employees' ID badges. Which training topic most directly addresses preventing this kind of exposure?
explanation: Operational security (OPSEC) training teaches employees to avoid exposing details about the organization's systems, people, and activities that an attacker could collect and combine. Password management covers credentials, removable media training covers drives and cables, and phishing campaigns test users' responses to simulated phishing.

question: An employee is working from a coffee shop and needs to reach an internal HR application. Which guidance for hybrid and remote work is most appropriate?

choices.a: Connect to the corporate VPN before accessing internal resources and keep the screen out of view of others
choices.b: Use the coffee shop's open Wi-Fi directly because the HR application requires a login
choices.c: Disable the laptop's host firewall to avoid connection problems on the public network
choices.d: Save the HR files to the desktop so they remain available offline

explanation: Remote work guidance tells users to protect traffic on untrusted networks with the company VPN and to guard against shoulder surfing in public places. A login page alone does not protect the rest of the traffic on an open network, disabling the host firewall exposes the laptop, and copying sensitive files locally increases the risk if the device is lost or stolen.

question: A company is launching a new security awareness program. Before any training is delivered, it sends a simulated phishing email to all staff and records the click and report rates. What is the main purpose of this step?

choices.a: To identify and discipline employees who click
choices.b: To establish an initial baseline so later results can show whether the program is working
choices.c: To meet the requirement for recurring annual training
choices.d: To replace the need for formal training content

explanation: Initial reporting and monitoring captures a starting baseline, so later recurring campaigns can measure improvement. Using results to punish employees discourages reporting, a single pre-training test is not recurring training, and simulations support training rather than replace it.

question: A security team is developing a new awareness program. Which approach is most effective?

choices.a: Buy one generic video and require every employee to watch it once
choices.b: Train only the IT department, since other staff do not manage systems
choices.c: Identify the organization's main risks and audiences, set learning objectives, and tailor content by role, such as payment fraud training for the finance team
choices.d: Wait until a security incident occurs and then build training around it

explanation: Developing an effective program starts with assessing risks and audiences, defining objectives, and tailoring content to the threats each role actually faces. One generic video ignores role-specific risks, training only IT leaves the most targeted users unprepared, and waiting for an incident makes the program reactive instead of preventive.

question: A security team has finished designing its awareness program and is now in the execution phase. Which activity belongs to execution?

choices.a: Rolling out training modules and phishing simulations on the planned schedule and tracking completion
choices.b: Identifying which departments face the greatest social engineering risk
choices.d: Choosing training topics based on recent incident trends

explanation: Execution is delivering the program: running the training and simulations as scheduled and tracking participation and results. Identifying high-risk departments, defining learning objectives, and choosing topics are all part of developing the program before it is delivered.
